newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Colombo sells controlling stake in plantation firm.
newsitem.headline: Colombo sells controlling stake in plantation firm.

text.p: Sri Lanka on Monday sold a 51 percent stake in Udapussellawa Plantations Ltd at 65.25 rupees per 10 rupee share, brokers said.

Plantation Investment & Management Co Ltd (PIMC), a joint venture between Merchant Bank of Sri Lanka Ltd, Insurance Corp, and the Employees' Trust Fund, bought the controlling stake in Udapussellawa on the stock exchange.
PIMC also bought a 51 percent stake in Hapugastenne Plantations Ltd when it was privatised through the stock exchange in late August.

This Udapussellawa transaction is highest per-share price for any state-owned plantation firm. However, the overall purchase price of 316 million rupees is below the 420.75 million paid for 51 percent of Balangoda Plantation Ltd, which was privatised last month.
The previous per-share high for a privatised plantation company was also Balangodo Plantation, which fetched 41.25 rupees per 10 rupee share.
Plantation companies have been popular among investors mainly because Sri Lanka tea prices have been near record highs recently, brokers said.

The government said last year it would sell controlling stakes in 23 plantation firms. Controlling interest in 13 have so far been sold with six, where the process has been completed, now trading on the bourse.
The government expects to complete privatisation of the plantation sector by the end of 1996, government officials said.
